terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the orders file here to see three carts go through, two of them with a mistake.

tasks.title: Refuse a quantity that makes no sense
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/orders.js`, make `lineTotal(candle, qty)` give what `qty` of the candle cost together, in cents. When `qty` is less than `1`, or not a whole number, it throws a `RangeError` whose message names the `qty` it was given.

Check calls `lineTotal` with good quantities and with wrong ones of its own, and looks at what it throws: an `Error`, of the kind `RangeError`, with the quantity in its message.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on throw and on picking the kind of error.
First ask whether `qty` is wrong, and throw when it is.
After that, return the price of one candle times `qty`.
Try `lineTotal(catalogue[0], 0)` at the bottom of the file and read what Node prints.
hints: Check the quantity before working anything out. Once an error is thrown, nothing after it in the function runs.
A quantity is not whole when rounding it down changes it: `Math.floor(qty)` is not `qty`. Put the qty in the message with a template literal.
The function starts with ``if (qty < 1 || Math.floor(qty) !== qty) { throw new RangeError(`The quantity must be 1 or more, not ${qty}`) }``, then `return candle.priceCents * qty`.

tasks.title: Refuse a candle the shop does not have
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make `findCandle(candles, sku)` give the candle of `candles` whose `sku` is `sku`. When there is none, it throws a `RangeError` whose message names the `sku` it was given.

Check calls `findCandle` with a list of its own, with skus that are in it and skus that are not, and an empty list, and looks at what it gives back or throws.
nextSteps: Find the candle with the list method that gives back the first match.
Throw when nothing was, and return the candle when something was.
Run the file: the last cart should now come back with a reason.
hints: `find` gives back `undefined` when nothing matches. Returning that would let the order go on with no candle.
Ask about `undefined` after the `find`, and throw there, where the problem is found, with the sku in the message.
The body is `const candle = candles.find((c) => c.sku === sku)`, then ``if (candle === undefined) { throw new RangeError(`No candle with the sku ${sku}`) }``, then `return candle`.

tasks.title: Let a wrong line pass up
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `cartTotal(candles, cart)` give what the whole cart costs, in cents: for each line, `findCandle` finds the candle and `lineTotal` works out the line, and the lines are added up. An empty cart costs `0`. When a line is wrong, the error that `findCandle` or `lineTotal` throws passes up out of `cartTotal` as it is: `cartTotal` does not catch it.

Check calls `cartTotal` with carts of its own, putting stand-ins in place of your `findCandle` and `lineTotal`, so this task does not depend on the two before it. A cart with a wrong line must end in the same error the stand-in threw.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on where to catch.
Start a total at 0 and go through the lines with `for...of`.
For each line, find the candle, work out the line, and add it.
Return the total. There is no `try` in this function.
hints: An error that nobody catches inside a function leaves it at once and goes on to whoever called it. That is exactly what this task wants.
Each line is `{ sku, qty }`. Hand `findCandle` the candles and the line's sku, then hand `lineTotal` what came back and the line's qty.
Inside `for (const line of cart)`, the line is `total = total + lineTotal(findCandle(candles, line.sku), line.qty)`.

tasks.title: Answer the customer, and only the customer
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make `placeOrder(candles, cart)` call `cartTotal` with the candles and the cart. For a good cart it gives `{ ok: true, totalCents }` with the total. When `cartTotal` throws a `RangeError`, it gives `{ ok: false, reason }`, where `reason` is the error's message. Any other error is a mistake in the code, which the customer cannot fix: `placeOrder` lets it pass, as it is.

Check puts a stand-in in place of your `cartTotal` that gives a total, throws a `RangeError`, throws a `TypeError` or throws a plain `Error`, and looks at what `placeOrder` does with each.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on telling one kind of error from another.
Call `cartTotal` inside `try`, and return the good answer from there.
In `catch`, ask whether the error is a `RangeError` and answer the customer when it is.
Throw every other error again, and run the file.
hints: This is the one place with something to do about a mistake in the order: tell the customer what was wrong. A mistake in the code is not theirs to fix.
`error instanceof RangeError` asks whether the error is of that kind. For any other error, `throw error` sends the same error on, as if `placeOrder` had not caught it.
The shape is `try { return { ok: true, totalCents: cartTotal(candles, cart) } } catch (error) { if (error instanceof RangeError) { return { ok: false, reason: error.message } } throw error }`.
